interactions.label: A 30-year-old woman with known rheumatic heart disease dies of cardiac failure 3

params.question: A 30-year-old woman with known rheumatic heart disease dies of cardiac failure 35 days after a normal vaginal delivery. How is this death classified?

answers.text: Direct obstetric death, because the cardiac failure occurred during the puerperal period

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Direct obstetric deaths result from complications of the pregnancy itself — haemorrhage, eclampsia, sepsis, obstructed labour — not from pre-existing conditions. The timing in the puerperium does not make a death 'direct.'

answers.text: Late maternal death, because it occurred more than four weeks after delivery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Late maternal deaths occur between 42 days and one year after pregnancy. At 35 days, this death falls within the standard 42-day window and counts toward the maternal mortality ratio.

answers.text: Indirect obstetric death, because a pre-existing condition was aggravated by pregnancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Rheumatic heart disease is a pre-existing condition aggravated by the haemodynamic demands of pregnancy. Death from it within 42 days of delivery is an indirect obstetric death.

answers.text: Coincidental death, because cardiac disease is not caused by pregnancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Coincidental deaths are from entirely unrelated causes such as road accidents. Cardiac disease worsened by pregnancy's physiological demands has a clear causal link and is classified as an indirect obstetric death.

overallFeedback.feedback: This is an indirect obstetric death — a pre-existing condition (rheumatic heart disease) worsened by pregnancy. Direct deaths come from pregnancy complications themselves; coincidental deaths are unrelated (e.g. accidents).
Well done. Indirect obstetric deaths occur when a pre-existing disease is aggravated by the physiological changes of pregnancy. In India, cardiac disease and anaemia are leading indirect causes.

interactions.label: A baby delivered at 30 weeks of gestation shows skin peeling, greenish-brown dis

params.question: A baby delivered at 30 weeks of gestation shows skin peeling, greenish-brown discolouration, and softened collapsed tissues. What type of stillbirth is this, and what does it indicate?

answers.text: Fresh stillbirth, indicating a sudden intrapartum event such as cord prolapse

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A fresh (intrapartum) stillbirth shows no signs of maceration — the skin is intact with no discolouration. The features described here (skin peeling, greenish-brown skin, collapsed tissues) indicate death occurred well before labour.

answers.text: Macerated stillbirth, indicating the foetus died in utero well before delivery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Skin peeling, greenish-brown discolouration, and collapsed soft tissues are hallmarks of maceration, indicating intrauterine death at least 12–24 hours before delivery, often due to placental insufficiency or cord complications.

answers.text: Fresh stillbirth, indicating chronic placental insufficiency over several weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Chronic placental insufficiency leads to gradual intrauterine death and maceration, not a fresh stillbirth. Fresh stillbirths result from sudden intrapartum events (cord prolapse, placental abruption) and lack the features described here.

answers.text: Macerated stillbirth, indicating death from an acute event during labour

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While the identification as macerated is correct, the interpretation is not. Maceration means death occurred well before labour began — not during it. Acute intrapartum events cause fresh stillbirths, not macerated ones.

overallFeedback.feedback: The described features — skin peeling, greenish-brown discolouration, and tissue collapse — are hallmarks of a macerated stillbirth, indicating the foetus died in utero well before delivery, usually from placental insufficiency or cord problems.

Correct. Macerated stillbirth indicates death occurred in utero before labour began, typically from chronic conditions such as placental insufficiency. Fresh (intrapartum) stillbirths, by contrast, are quality-of-care markers because many are preventable.

interactions.label: A district hospital's caesarean section rate is 32%. Caesarean audit primarily h

params.question: A district hospital's caesarean section rate is 32%. Caesarean audit primarily helps the facility determine whether this rate reflects:

answers.text: Surgical complications occurring during individual caesarean procedures

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Audit of individual surgical complications is a different exercise. Facility-level caesarean audit examines the overall rate and what drives it — clinical indications versus non-clinical pressures.

answers.text: Genuine clinical need versus non-clinical pressures such as litigation fears or patient preference

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Caesarean audit uses the WHO benchmark of 10–15% as a reference to determine whether a facility's rate reflects genuine obstetric indications or non-clinical drivers such as patient preference, fear of litigation, staffing gaps, or financial incentives.

answers.text: The total maternal mortality directly attributable to caesarean delivery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Maternal mortality is tracked through separate indicators. Caesarean audit focuses on whether the indications for the operations were appropriate, not on counting deaths from the procedure.

answers.text: Whether the facility should eliminate caesarean sections and promote only vaginal deliveries

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Caesarean section is a life-saving intervention. The goal of audit is not to eliminate it but to ensure the rate is driven by clinical need rather than avoidable non-clinical factors.

overallFeedback.feedback: Caesarean audit compares a facility's CS rate against the WHO benchmark (10–15%) to determine whether the rate reflects genuine clinical need or is being driven by non-clinical pressures such as patient demand, fear of litigation, or financial incentives.

Exactly. The WHO benchmark of 10–15% helps identify facilities where the CS rate may be inflated by non-clinical pressures rather than genuine medical need. Structured audit using the Robson classification pinpoints which patient groups drive the excess.

interactions.label: Under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), pregnant women receive a direct c

params.question: Under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), pregnant women receive a direct cash payment to encourage institutional delivery.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: JSSK does not provide cash payments. It removes costs entirely — free delivery (including caesarean), drugs, diagnostics, meals, blood, and transport for the mother, and free treatment for sick newborns up to 30 days. The cash incentive for institutional delivery is under JSY, not JSSK.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. JSSK (launched 2011) eliminates costs by providing free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, meals, blood transfusion, and transport — it does not give cash. The direct cash incentive for institutional delivery is under JSY (launched 2005).

interactions.label: A woman has just delivered by caesarean section and is being prepared for discha

params.question: A woman has just delivered by caesarean section and is being prepared for discharge. Which documentation is essential in her delivery record for facility-level obstetric audit?

answers.text: A detailed account of the anaesthesia technique and intraoperative blood loss

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Anaesthetic and operative details are part of the surgical record, but for obstetric quality audit every delivery must be assigned its Robson group at discharge using six specific data elements recorded prospectively.

answers.text: Her Robson group classification based on parity, previous caesarean status, presentation, onset of labour, gestational age, and number of foetuses

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Every delivery must be assigned a Robson group at the time of discharge. These six obstetric characteristics must be recorded prospectively so the classification can drive meaningful caesarean audit.

answers.text: A formal maternal near-miss assessment score regardless of whether complications occurred

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Near-miss assessment uses WHO organ-dysfunction criteria and applies only to women who survived a life-threatening complication — it is not a routine discharge requirement for every delivery.

answers.text: A completed Janani Suraksha Yojana application with bank account details

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Checking programme eligibility is a separate clinical responsibility (programme enrollment). The Robson group classification is the specific delivery-record documentation needed for facility-level obstetric audit.

overallFeedback.feedback: Every delivery must be assigned a Robson group at discharge using six data elements: parity, previous CS status, fetal presentation, onset of labour, gestational age, and number of foetuses. This prospective documentation is essential for facility-level caesarean audit.

Well done. Prospective Robson classification at discharge is a core clinical responsibility. Without accurate, real-time recording of these six characteristics, facility-level caesarean audit cannot function.
